skill.name: limrun-maestro-testing
skill.description: Run and debug Maestro YAML flows on Limrun cloud iOS simulators from Linux, Windows, macOS, virtual machines, or containers. Supports suite migration, CI execution, Expo workflows, artifact collection, and selector troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Run Maestro UI tests on remote Limrun iOS simulators.
skill.author: limrun-inc

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown formatting, protocol examples, instance identifiers, or defensive credential guidance. The curl-to-shell installer is a confirmed critical supply-chain risk. The workflow also transfers application builds and test activity to Limrun cloud infrastructure.

remediation.issue: The Maestro installation command downloads remote content and executes it directly with Bash.
remediation.suggestion: Use a pinned release artifact, verify its checksum or signature, and run a reviewed installer file separately.

remediation.issue: Application builds and test interactions are processed on third-party cloud simulators.
remediation.suggestion: Document Limrun data handling and advise users to use approved builds, synthetic test data, and scoped credentials.

content.user_title: Run Maestro Tests on Limrun iOS
content.value_statement: Local iOS infrastructure limits Maestro testing across development and CI environments. This skill guides remote setup, execution, diagnosis, artifact capture, and cleanup through Limrun.
actual_capabilities: Checks Limrun, Maestro, and Java prerequisites before testing.
Creates a remote iOS simulator and validates it with the Settings app.
Runs individual Maestro flows or directories against a selected iOS instance.
Configures app packages, Expo Go, and Expo development client workflows.
Explains logs, selector failures, screenshots, UI hierarchies, and output artifacts.
Coordinates recording and instance cleanup around Maestro runs.
limitations: Supports Limrun iOS simulators only, not Android devices or local simulators.
Requires Limrun authentication, the Limrun CLI, Maestro CLI, and Java 17 or newer.
Maestro recording commands, addMedia, and local simulator file references are unsupported.
Remote execution depends on Limrun service availability and approved handling of application data.

use_cases.title: Validate mobile user journeys
use_cases.description: Run repeatable Maestro flows on remote iOS simulators and inspect failures with screenshots and accessibility data.

use_cases.title: Debug Expo interfaces
use_cases.description: Open Expo projects on cloud simulators and refine selectors for stable iOS automation.

use_cases.title: Move tests into CI
use_cases.description: Target explicit simulator instances, preserve reports, record runs, and clean up resources after execution.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a basic setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify my Limrun Maestro setup using the iOS Settings app, then explain each validation result.

prompt_templates.title: Run a project flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the Maestro flow at [path] on iOS instance [id], preserve artifacts, and summarize failures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Routine local or remote test execution

prompt_templates.title: Debug a selector
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this failing Maestro selector using the live element tree and recommend a stable accessibility-based replacement: [failure].

prompt_templates.title: Migrate a CI suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my Maestro suite at [path] for Limrun CI, including instance targeting, tagging, output directories, recording, and cleanup.

output_examples.input: Verify Maestro against the Settings app on a new Limrun iOS instance.
output: The simulator was created with the Maestro runner available.
The Settings flow completed and captured a screenshot.
The remote driver connection is ready for application testing.

output_examples.input: Explain why my text selector fails on the remote simulator.
output_examples.output: The visible text differs from the accessibility label. Inspect the live element tree, then match the exact stable label.

output_examples.input: Prepare my smoke suite for CI execution.
output_examples.output: The suite uses an explicit instance, smoke tags, a dedicated artifact directory, optional recording, preserved exit codes, and final resource cleanup.

best_practices: Use explicit iOS instance identifiers in scripts and CI jobs.
Anchor assertions on stable accessibility identifiers or exact labels.
Use approved test builds, synthetic data, and scoped credentials on remote simulators.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers directly into a shell without integrity verification.
Do not pass driver or platform flags that Limrun manages automatically.
Do not depend on fixed delays or unsupported local simulator file paths.

faq.question: Does this skill support Android testing?
faq.answer: No. It supports Maestro flows on Limrun iOS simulators only.

faq.question: Which Maestro versions are supported?
faq.answer: The documented Limrun runner supports Maestro 2.5 through 2.7.

faq.question: Can I use this in CI?
faq.answer: Yes. Specify the simulator instance, preserve output artifacts, and use Maestro exit codes for job status.

faq.question: Does it support Expo applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Expo Go and development client flows using project or client links.

faq.question: Where are screenshots saved?
faq.answer: Maestro saves screenshots in the working directory or the selected test output directory.

faq.question: How should I handle secrets?
faq.answer: Use scoped Limrun credentials and synthetic test accounts. Never place production secrets in flows, logs, prompts, or artifacts.
